problem: The three win patterns are dead rules: games end by Long Night (deck runs out), not by a pattern.
evidence: Strategic mirror, 2000 games per count: Long Night 95.2% / 99.9% / 100% at 2/3/4p. Pattern wins: 2p mass 96, constellation 1, alignment 0; 3p mass 1; 4p none. A pattern is formed ~21 times per 2p game but survives to the owner's next turn 0.2% of the time (0.0% at 3-4p). Oracle probe (perfect information about the next opponent's hand): a pattern-forming plan that the next opponent cannot break exists in 5 of 573 positions (2p), 5 of 547 (3p), 1 of 462 (4p).
fix: The 'must survive a round' clause is the cause (every spin crashes, so a full orbit always loses a body). Tested: check the win at the END of your own turn (after Spin and Crash). 3p becomes 20 turns, Long Night 12.5%, shares mass 42 / alignment 39 / constellation 5%. It is not a clean fix: 2p drops to 4.9 turns (instant wins), 4p keeps 58% Long Night. Needs a per-count knob, for example a Critical Mass threshold of 17+ at 2p, or 5 slots/opening bodies of 1.

problem: Games are about 3x too long and the stated turn cap is false.
evidence: Mean turns 46.2 / 46.7 / 39.6 (2/3/4p) vs the rules' bands 14-24 / 18-30 / 20-34. At 0.4 min per turn (assumption) that is 18.5 / 18.7 / 15.8 min vs 12 target (9.6-14.4). Rules 6 says at most 43/38/33 turns, but taking from Deep Space does not shrink the Deck: 94% / 99% / 99% of games exceed the stated cap (max 60 / 71 / 54).
fix: Make the clock real: end Long Night when the Deck is empty OR after a fixed number of rounds, remove 12-16 cards from the Deck at setup, or count Deep Space draws toward the clock. Correct the stated cap.

problem: Churn: the board is rebuilt every turn and nothing is kept; the result is decided in the last rounds before the deck runs out.
evidence: 58.7 / 43.3 / 29.8 captures per game (about 1.3 per turn at 2p); 96.6% / 93.7% / 89.3% of spins cause at least one crash; 21.0 / 28.6 / 22.9 lead changes per game (leader by orbit total); midpoint leader wins 51.3% / 35.1% / 23.3% (fair: 50 / 33 / 25), so there is no runaway but also nothing that accumulates. Spins are very kinetic; the cost is that no plan survives.
fix: Reduce captures per spin: tested one-contact crash (only the contact on the side you spin towards): captures fall 25-35% but formed patterns still never survive (survival 0.4%). Better untested ideas: captured cards go to Deep Space not the hand; a body that just arrived cannot be captured until its owner's next turn (shield marker); or crashes only happen on the contacts of the active player's own orbit.

problem: The best bot play is 'maximise total Size at deck-out', not pattern building; the pattern-chasing strategic bot loses to greedy at 4 players.
evidence: Strategic vs greedy win gap: +38.0 (2p), +15.7 (3p), -5.5 (4p). Both beat random by 97-100 points, which only shows that some play beats random. Bot-dependent skill reading (L2): skill in the intended direction is unproven at 3-4p.
fix: Fix the win conditions first (problem 1), then re-measure with the same three bots.

problem: Rebound is not a comeback device; it is a permanent state that adds churn.
evidence: Without Rebound the midpoint-leader rate is 52.5% / 38.9% / 22.2% vs 51.3% / 35.1% / 23.3% with it (no change); lead changes fall from 21.0 to 15.9 (2p). With it a player has Rebound on 32 of ~46 turns at 2p (about 70% of their turns), because captures keep emptying orbits.
fix: Drop Rebound or limit it (once per game, or only when 2+ bodies behind). Measure after the clock fix; at present it fails the inert-twist test for comeback (L1).

problem: Deep Space and Recall are marginal at 3-4 players; only spin-any-orbit and the Comet rule clearly matter.
evidence: Ablation margin vs full strategic bot (2p / 3p / 4p, 400 games each, +-5): self-spin-only +10.5 / +18.2 / +10.0 (pass); comet-blind +82.7 / +19.1 / +19.2 (pass); no-recall +18.3 / +2.0 / -4.0 (fails at 3-4p); deck-only -5.2 / +8.0 / -2.9 (fails at 2p and 4p: taking from Deep Space does not help). Under win_at_end+one_contact: self-spin +34.0 / +32.5 / +25.7, deck-only -2.0 / +2.0 / +8.0, no-recall +1.3 / +5.0 / +10.3.
fix: Keep spin-any-orbit and Comet beats Giant. Cut or sharpen Deep Space (e.g. take both top cards, or only the last discard of a rival) and decide whether Recall earns its slot; re-run after the win-timing fix.

problem: Long Night ties are common at 3-4 players and Comets never reach the end orbit.
evidence: Shared wins 4.7% (3p) and 7.8% (4p). Size 1 average count in the final orbit is 0.14 for winners and 0.14 for losers (2p): no link to winning, while Sizes 4-5 average 1.1-1.3 in winners' orbits vs 0.45-0.63 for losers.
fix: Add a second tie-break (fewest cards in hand, or largest single body).
